items.text: Our programmes and projects
Sightsavers runs programmes in eye health, neglected tropical diseases and disability rights. Here, you can explore a selection of our current and recent projects.
On this page
On this page
Current programmes
Focus on Clear Vision
Sightsavers is providing free vision tests, eye health checks and pairs of glasses in Nigeria and Kenya, as part of Bloomberg Philanthropies’ Vision Initiative.
Reaching the Last Mile Fund
Sightsavers is working with partners across Africa to support countries to eliminate onchocerciasis and lymphatic filariasis.
Accelerate programme
The Accelerate trachoma elimination programme aims to support at least 15 countries to eliminate trachoma as a public health risk, and speed up progress in two others by 2027.
RISE/E initiative
This initiative, Ready for Inclusive Sustainable Employment and Entrepreneurship, tackles inequality and promotes economic inclusion for young people with disabilities.
WISH2 programme
The second phase of the Women’s Integrated Sexual Health (WISH2) programme aims to build inclusive and sustainable sexual and reproductive health systems in West and Central Africa.
Improving health and nutrition in schools
This programme, known as SHIP, checks schoolchildren for health problems and refers them for treatment.
Tusambilile Chapamo
We’re improving educational opportunities for children and young people with disabilities in Zambia by increasing access to equitable and inclusive education.
Inclusive eye health
Sightsavers advocates for universal health coverage, so everyone, wherever they live, can access quality, affordable health care when they need it.
Using technology to fight disease
Sightsavers is pioneering new ways to use technology as part of programmes to tackle avoidable blindness.
Uganda inclusive education project
Sightsavers is working with the Ugandan government to improve inclusive education across the country.
Recent programmes
Sierra Leone education programme
The programme, which ended in 2026, aimed to make secondary secondary schools more inclusive and accessible for all students, especially girls and children with disabilities.
Inclusive Futures
This programme tested innovative ways to improve economic empowerment and inclusion for people with disabilities, enabling them to earn a living, access quality healthcare and get an education.
WISH1 programme

The first phase of the Women’s Integrated Sexual Health (WISH1) programme aimed to increase access to sexual and reproductive health and rights services for women in West and Central Africa. It ran from 2018 to 2024.
DISSECT project: putting people first in the elimination of onchocerciasis
This four-year research initiative explored new tools to help eliminate the parasitic infection river blindness.
Onchocerciasis elimination mapping project
We worked with our partners in Ghana and Nigeria to devise new ways to collect valuable data about the spread and transmission of river blindness.
Connecting the Dots

This employment programme provided vocational training courses for people with disabilities in western Uganda, helping to transform attitudes within the local community and create more inclusive workplaces.
The Commonwealth Fund
This two-year programme funded trachoma operations, treatment and improved hygiene and sanitation across 10 countries in the Commonwealth.
Super School of Five
This programme introduced superhero characters to schoolchildren in Kenya, Ethiopia, Zambia and Nigeria to encourage better hygiene, to help eliminate trachoma.
Ascend: fighting disease in Africa
This programme was Sightsavers’ largest multiple neglected tropical disease programme to date. It launched in 2019 and closed in August 2021.
Keep Sight
To tackle glaucoma in India and Nigeria, Sightsavers worked with pharmaceutical company AbbVie and the International Agency for the Prevention of Blindness.
Seeing is Believing
This 17-year-long project worked to treat avoidable blindness and improve local healthcare. It reached more than 34 million people living in Africa and Asia.
The Right to Health
This programme focused on restoring sight and making health services accessible for marginalised groups in Pakistan and Bangladesh.
SAFE: trachoma control
Sightsavers’ trachoma control programme, which came to an end in 2019, helped to protect more than 18 million people.
UNITED in Nigeria
This six-year UNITED programme, funded by UK aid, delivered more than 158 million treatments in Nigeria to tackle neglected tropical diseases.
A Million Miracles
Thanks to your support, between 2014 and 2017 our fundraising campaign raised enough money to provide a million sight-saving cataract operations.
Reducing LF and river blindness
Our programme, which ran from 2016 to 2019, provided medication to protect people at risk of river blindness and lymphatic filariasis.
Coordinated Approach to Community Health (CATCH)
We wanted to ensure that patients visiting our trachoma screening camps could also be treated for other eye conditions.
The Global Trachoma Mapping Project (GTMP)
The project gathered a wealth of valuable data about the world’s trachoma-endemic areas using smartphones.
Inclusive education in Senegal
This pilot project showed that children with and without disabilities can learn together.
Trachoma Initiative
The five-year programme provided millions of sight-saving treatments to help eliminate trachoma in seven countries.
Bhopal inclusive eye health project
Sightsavers’ pilot project in India aimed to ensure that everyone can access eye health services.
Our programme evaluations
